Title: Mandarin Program Flourishes at Crossroads
Chunks: 0
Among a wall of comics, images, and fun memes on learning Mandarin, Diana Corey’s classroom displays a poster of the language’s one thousand most widely used characters. The dedicated Crossroads students who take Mandarin have a goal of eventually learning these and more (Diana herself knows between 4,000-5,000 characters). As the most widely spoken language in the world and the main dialect of the Chinese language, Mandarin is growing in popularity among Crossroads students. There are seven courses being taught this year, ranging from Mandarin A and B for middle school students, to Mandarin 1-5 for high school.
“Students who take Mandarin are up for the challenge,” says Diana Corey, Crossroads’ Mandarin teacher for the past seven years. “It takes a certain level of commitment to learn a new language and with Mandarin, students are learning how to write individual characters in addition to the typical reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills that go with learning a foreign language.”
Mandarin students also have the unique opportunity to build community across difference and gain a deeper understanding of Chinese culture. The Chinese Club meets weekly and includes native Chinese students through our partnership with the Cambridge Institute. “Our native Chinese speakers are excited to support our Mandarin students as tutors and through cultural exchange with the Chinese Club,” Diana adds. The Chinese Club meets weekly and engages students around language and culture, including pop culture, food, and holiday celebrations.
Diana and her classes have also formed a unique connection with a Chinese orphanage network. In a student-driven service project, groups contribute their time to Chinese-English translation of reports to adopted families who sponsor the children from the United States. Students also write in Chinese to prospective Crossroads students in China describing the school and a typical day at Crossroads.
Students also have the opportunity to build their Mandarin skills through immersion; every two years Diana brings a group of students to China. The next group will be forming for a visit this summer. “Our students get more engaged with the language as they go through the program and we try to keep it fun and connect to culture through Chinese art, cooking, and celebration of festivals.”

# K-8 Mandarin Chinese/English Immersion Program
**Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Principal: Gerald Yung**
Putnam Ave Upper School, Phanenca Babio-James
100 Putnam Street
Cambridge, MA 02139
617.349.6562
mlk.cpsd.us
The Preschool-8 Mandarin Chinese/English Immersion Program is one of only two Mandarin Chinese dual language programs in a Public School in New England. It is open to all students in the Cambridge Public Schools (subject to availability). The program is designed for native Mandarin Chinese speakers, bilingual and heritage Mandarin speakers as well as native English speakers to develop speaking, listening, reading and writing skills in both languages while realizing their academic potential in all of their academic subjects. The program delivers rigorous, grade level instruction in both languages daily. Within day-to-day learning, we celebrate the cultures and traditions where Mandarin is the official language or a dominant language including Mainland China, Taiwan, Singapore, Hong Kong, Macau, Malaysia and Tibet.

# K-8 Mandarin Chinese/English Immersion Program
**Dr. Martin Luther King Jr., Principal: Gerald Yung**
Putnam Ave Upper School, Phanenca Babio-James
100 Putnam Street
Cambridge, MA 02139
617.349.6562
mlk.cpsd.us
The Preschool-8 Mandarin Chinese/English Immersion Program is one of only two Mandarin Chinese dual language programs in a Public School in New England. It is open to all students in the Cambridge Public Schools (subject to availability). The program is designed for native Mandarin Chinese speakers, bilingual and heritage Mandarin speakers as well as native English speakers to develop speaking, listening, reading and writing skills in both languages while realizing their academic potential in all of their academic subjects. The program delivers rigorous, grade level instruction in both languages daily. Within day-to-day learning, we celebrate the cultures and traditions where Mandarin is the official language or a dominant language including Mainland China, Taiwan, Singapore, Hong Kong, Macau, Malaysia and Tibet.
剑桥公立学校的Preschool-8中文/英文沉浸项目是新英格兰地区两个中文双语项目的其中一个。这个项目是开放给所有剑桥公立学校的学生（视空位而定）。该项目旨在培养母语为中文的学生、双语者、以及中文族裔语言学习者和母语为英文的学生，在所有学科中发展中文和英文的口语、听力、阅读和写作能力，实现他们在学业上的潜能。此项目每天都提供严谨的、符合年级水平的双语教学。在日常学习中，我们用心地利用各种教学决策来提升那些使用中文为官方语言或主要语言的文化和传统（包括中国大陆、台湾、新加坡、香港、澳门、马来西亚和西藏），这使得该项目与一般的教育课堂有所区别。

Among a wall of comics, images, and fun memes on learning Mandarin, Diana Corey’s classroom displays a poster of the language’s one thousand most widely used characters. The dedicated Crossroads students who take Mandarin have a goal of eventually learning these and more (Diana herself knows between 4,000-5,000 characters). As the most widely spoken language in the world and the main dialect of the Chinese language, Mandarin is growing in popularity among Crossroads students. There are seven courses being taught this year, ranging from Mandarin A and B for middle school students, to Mandarin 1-5 for high school.
“Students who take Mandarin are up for the challenge,” says Diana Corey, Crossroads’ Mandarin teacher for the past seven years. “It takes a certain level of commitment to learn a new language and with Mandarin, students are learning how to write individual characters in addition to the typical reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills that go with learning a foreign language.”
Mandarin students also have the unique opportunity to build community across difference and gain a deeper understanding of Chinese culture. The Chinese Club meets weekly and includes native Chinese students through our partnership with the Cambridge Institute. “Our native Chinese speakers are excited to support our Mandarin students as tutors and through cultural exchange with the Chinese Club,” Diana adds. The Chinese Club meets weekly and engages students around language and culture, including pop culture, food, and holiday celebrations.
Diana and her classes have also formed a unique connection with a Chinese orphanage network. In a student-driven service project, groups contribute their time to Chinese-English translation of reports to adopted families who sponsor the children from the United States. Students also write in Chinese to prospective Crossroads students in China describing the school and a typical day at Crossroads.
Students also have the opportunity to build their Mandarin skills through immersion; every two years Diana brings a group of students to China. The next group will be forming for a visit this summer. “Our students get more engaged with the language as they go through the program and we try to keep it fun and connect to culture through Chinese art, cooking, and celebration of festivals.”

The Preschool-8 Mandarin Chinese/English Immersion Program is one of only two Mandarin Chinese dual language programs in a Public School in New England. It is open to all students in the Cambridge Public Schools (subject to availability). The program is designed for native Mandarin Chinese speakers, bilingual and heritage Mandarin speakers as well as native English speakers to develop speaking, listening, reading and writing skills in both languages while realizing their academic potential in all of their academic subjects. The program delivers rigorous, grade level instruction in both languages daily. Within day-to-day learning, we celebrate the cultures and traditions where Mandarin is the official language or a dominant language including Mainland China, Taiwan, Singapore, Hong Kong, Macau, Malaysia and Tibet.

Title: Mandarin Program Flourishes at Crossroads

Among a wall of comics, images, and fun memes on learning Mandarin, Diana Corey’s classroom displays a poster of the language’s one thousand most widely used characters. The dedicated Crossroads students who take Mandarin have a goal of eventually learning these and more (Diana herself knows between 4,000-5,000 characters). As the most widely spoken language in the world and the main dialect of the Chinese language, Mandarin is growing in popularity among Crossroads students. There are seven courses being taught this year, ranging from Mandarin A and B for middle school students, to Mandarin 1-5 for high school.
“Students who take Mandarin are up for the challenge,” says Diana Corey, Crossroads’ Mandarin teacher for the past seven years. “It takes a certain level of commitment to learn a new language and with Mandarin, students are learning how to write individual characters in addition to the typical reading, writing, speaking, and listening skills that go with learning a foreign language.”
Mandarin students also have the unique opportunity to build community across difference and gain a deeper understanding of Chinese culture. The Chinese Club meets weekly and includes native Chinese students through our partnership with the Cambridge Institute. “Our native Chinese speakers are excited to support our Mandarin students as tutors and through cultural exchange with the Chinese Club,” Diana adds. The Chinese Club meets weekly and engages students around language and culture, including pop culture, food, and holiday celebrations.
Diana and her classes have also formed a unique connection with a Chinese orphanage network. In a student-driven service project, groups contribute their time to Chinese-English translation of reports to adopted families who sponsor the children from the United States. Students also write in Chinese to prospective Crossroads students in China describing the school and a typical day at Crossroads.
Students also have the opportunity to build their Mandarin skills through immersion; every two years Diana brings a group of students to China. The next group will be forming for a visit this summer. “Our students get more engaged with the language as they go through the program and we try to keep it fun and connect to culture through Chinese art, cooking, and celebration of festivals.”

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### St Mary's School, Cambridge is an all-girls, all-through day and boarding school that offers an education rooted in the Catholic faith to students with a broad range of abilities. The only all-girls school in Cambridge, St Mary's has a large international boarding community from Year 5.
Located in central Cambridge, St Mary's enrols a total of 650 girls aged three to 18 years. It has 120 years' expertise in educating girls, saying that "From teaching and pastoral care to school life, everything at St Mary’s is built for girls".
As a member of the Girls’ School Association (GSA), it is _proud of its high numbers of girls studying STEM subjects. In 2019,43.6% studied maths compared to 8.1% nationally, and 35.9% studies biology compared to 9.9% nationally._
The school has _dedicated campuses for its Junior School, Senior School and Sixth Form_ (all within walking distance of each other) offering parents the advantage of an all-through education, as well as smaller learning communities for each stage of their child's learning.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### St Mary's School, Cambridge is an all-girls, all-through day and boarding school that offers an education rooted in the Catholic faith to students with a broad range of abilities. The only all-girls school in Cambridge, St Mary's has a large international boarding community from Year 5.
_St Mary's is proud of its international student community (around 20% of students are from overseas, representing over 30 different countries) and this is felt throughout the school corridors._ A noticeboard displays information relating to different countries, cultures, and identities across the world; a giant map in the dining room displays the countries of origin of students at the school; and girls connect with students worldwide through‘E-twinning’ with other schools and sharing virtual classrooms.
While St Mary's is a Catholic school, it does welcome girls of all faiths and secular backgrounds. All students will be expected to attend weekly lessons in religious studies until Year 11 and complete their GCSE in the subject.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Curriculum
Teaching follows a blended curriculum that enriches the National Curriculum for England with _specialist teaching from a young age and a cross-curricular approach to subjects including science, art, geography, and music._
As girls move up the school, the curriculum is split into pre-GCSE (Years 7 -9), GCSE curriculum (Years 10-11), and A Levels (Years 12-13).
There's _a strong focus on science and maths here with students working on STEM-related topics from Reception_. The school has also been recognised by the UK Association for the Promotion of Chinese Education (UKAPCE) as one of the ‘Best Schools’ for Mandarin in the UK. Students learn Mandarin during lessons, as well as other traditions such as art and calligraphy, drama and singing.
What are the fees?

There are also many extra-curricular clubs focusing on STEM, and scholarships for excellence in Textiles, STEM, and Design and Enterprise.
While St Mary's is a selective school, it does welcome a broad ability range. Compared to the very academically rigorous and selective nature of the neighbouring Perse School, _St Mary's offers a more relaxed learning environment that will certainly suit some girls more than others._
Girls are taught to have great self-belief in their abilities; _whatever their starting point, they are taught to work hard and aim high. HPL, or High Performance Learning, is embedded in the curriculum throughout the school._ This framework of teaching focuses on advanced thinking skills and learning behaviours to help build 'better brains' – and this is key to the school's message to all learners that they _will_ succeed.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Sport and the arts
St Mary's is often talked about more for the arts than sport, although there are opportunities to study both as part of the curriculum and as extra-curricular activities.
_All girls study drama in Years 7 and 8, and can take it as an option at GCSE and A Level._ Highlights in the arts calendar include an outdoor Shakespeare production every year. And there are plenty of extra-curricular clubs (15 of these are dedicated to music every week).Facilities include an art and photography centre, which has four art teaching spaces, a Sixth Form study space, a dark room and a photography studio.
Sport at St Mary's _is driven by a 'sports for all' policy, and focuses on the relationship between sport and "self-worth, confidence and body image in young girls"._ While girls still compete in sports including netball, rowing (it is Cambridge after all, and the school does have its own boathouse) and swimming, there are plenty of opportunities to play and enjoy non-performance activities such as boxercise, gymnastics and Zumba. The school has expanded its sports programme to include many solo pursuits than can be enjoyed for life, with less 'traditional' sports such as kung fu and dance.

Other sporting highlights include an annual Girls’ Schools Association (GSA) Gymnastics Display and a Holland hockey trip (Years 9 and 10).
_Most sports facilities are located off campus at the recently opened Long Road sports ground_, but the Senior School does have its own gymnasium, outdoor gym, table tennis, netball and tennis courts.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Academic results
Results at St Mary's are impressive. In 2021, 35% of A Level grades were A*, 81% were A*-A, and 97% were A*-B. 100% were A*- C grades.Subject highlights include particularly strong performances in Spanish, Drama, Further Maths, Music, Greek and Latin with 100% of grades at A*.
In GCSEs, 47% of grades were A*, 66% of were A*-A, and 92% were A*- B grades. At least half of all students gained a grade 9 in the following subjects: History (53%), Art (50%), Class Civ (57%), Latin (55%) and Classical Greek (60%). In Music, 100% grades were the top 9 or 8.
_A measure of its success in helping girls of all abilities reach their goals can be seen in its Value Add results._ In 2021, the school's Value Add scores for GCSE and A Level was 0.7, which means that (on average) it added 0.7 of a grade to every girl's results, across all subjects; this could be the difference between 10 Grade 8s and 10 Grade 9s at GCSE.
_75% of St Mary's subject departments recorded Value Added scores placing them in the top 10% of schools,_ while physics, religious studies and Spanish all achieved the highest value-added scores in the UK.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Campus and facilities
St Mary's is investing in facilities for all students. Most recently it opened new sporting facilities at the nearby Long Road sports ground, including athletics facilities,AstroTurf pitches for hockey, rugby and football, cricket nets, and netball and tennis courts. A new STEM learning lab will open shortly.

The dedicated Sixth Form has subject classrooms, a silent study room, a social study and computer room, a career and Higher Education advice suite, spacious common room and a gym/dance studio.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### **Boarding**
Students can board from Year 5, and the majority who do come from overseas. _The school has one boarding house,Mary Ward House, which is within walking distance of the three schools_. There are around 90+ places available for Years 5-13 boarders, and families are advised to apply early as spaces are limited.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Admission and fees
Junior School applicants are assessed throughout the year;Senior School applicants attend an assessment day at the end of January; and Sixth Form applicants receive an offer made on their predicted grades.
_International applicants aged 9.5 years and older take the online UKiset test,_ which is designed for international applicants to British independent schools. UK applicants sit assessments for Years 3 and above.
St Mary's is not a highly selective school though, and _girls with a broad range of academic abilities are offered places. Top grades and academic achievement may not guarantee you a place here as the focus is more on evidence of "individual potential"._
Annual fees range from £10,923 for Reception to Year 2, to £17,031 for Years 7-13. Boarding fees start at £27,600 for Years 5-6 up to £35,301 for Years 7-13.

Title: St Mary’s School on Why There is Still a Place For Single-Sex Education
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
Last year an article examined the future of single-sex schooling and questioned if all-girls schools are a dying breed. The piece followed the news that Scotland’s last all-girls state school has begun enrolling boys. Scotland now has just six single-sex mainstream private schools, and numbers in England are also declining.
Government figures from 2002 showed England had 335 independent all-girls’ schools and 231 girls’ state schools. In 2022 that number fell to 232 and 213 respectively. So, does this downward trend mean single-sex education is outdated and unnecessary?
At St Mary’s School we would argue to the contrary. There are countless benefits to an all-girls education and, until we live in a world where gender inequalities do not exist, we must prepare our girls accordingly.
*   To teach academic subject knowledge, skills and understanding of the wider world and to look outward. This is relatively straight-forward with good teachers and appropriate facilities.

*   To teach self-knowledge and self-understanding and help each individual develop self-worth.
Both of these aspects of education – but particularly the latter – are determined by having the right kind of school culture in place plus a well-defined ethos and mission alongside superb pastoral skills and dedicated tutors. Many schools, especially those originally founded to educate boys, have a distinctly male culture focused on hierarchy and competition. Some girls thrive in this kind of environment. For others a culture focused on equality and cooperation feels more comfortable and nurturing.
Findings from the 2022 Sunday Times Parent Power rankings back this up. Figures released in December – which compared 2022 A-level and GCSE results with those from 2019 – showed that both private and state single-sex girl schools topped the academic league tables. Additionally, research from South Korea entitled ‘Non-Cognitive Consequences of Single-Sex Schooling’ found that single-sex education improves non-cognitive outcomes for students – particularly girls.
St Mary's School
So, what does St Mary’s School offer? Well, we’ve been educating and empowering girls since 1898, developing engaged, compassionate young women with the aspirations, confidence, and integrity to be themselves and help shape a better world.

From the moment they start at St Mary’s, our girls are taught to dream big and strive to reach their full potential. Supporting and challenging them in equal measure, we encourage them to believe anything is possible and nothing is out of their reach. Through High Performance Learning (HPL), we teach them to understand how they learn, as well as what they learn. The result is excellent academic outcomes and young adults who are curious, community-minded, resilient, and ready to go out and make a positive contribution to society.
Within Cambridge, St Mary’s School all-girls offering is unique. We excel at educating girls, and others agree. Our first-class education status was recently reinforced when we received the highest grade of ‘excellent’ in our ISI (Independent Schools Inspectorate) inspection. We achieved ‘excellent’ in both aspects of the Education Quality Inspection, covering academic achievements and personal development; inspectors praised the quality of our teaching; and parents gave us an outstanding overall satisfaction rate of 98%.
In 2022, we saw an incredibly successful return to public examinations with 66% of GCSE grades awarded at A* or A (9 – 7) and 72% of A-levels at grades A* to B. Our international sixth form students recently received outstanding results in their International English Language Testing System (IELTS) examinations.
We’ve also been named one of the best places to study Mandarin in the UK. Inspectors noted at our recent ISI Inspection that: _‘_Pupils make strong progress across the range of subjects’ and are: ‘…highly successful in their achievements beyond the classroom in a range of activities encompassing different interests.’
St Mary's School
The secret to our success is student happiness. We know contented girls accomplish so much more and ensure our pastoral care is second-to-none. Our approach is grounded in love, respect and trust and delivered in a secure environment where students are encouraged to gain a sense of their own worth. When it comes to emotional well-being, students have access to a fully-trained school counsellor, who offers confidential advice.

We also have a Lay Chaplain, who provides a listening ear and wise counsel when needed. The school has an independent listener, who is there for students should they wish to talk to an adult that is independent of the school. Our Senior School pupils can also use our ‘Wellbeing Room’ – immersing themselves in a range of activities and drop-in sessions, in a relaxing space that was designed by our student-led Wellbeing Committee.
At St Mary’s School, all subjects are ‘for girls’. In a nurturing, supportive environment, students are encouraged to pursue their interests, with no academic path off limits. We offer a space where the intellectual and social confidence of our students can blossom and where they can discover what motivates them – supported by excellent careers advice and work experience opportunities.
We work particularly hard to instil them with a passion for maths and science; subjects that girls have historically been less keen to pursue, particularly in co-ed settings.
St Mary's School
We embed a passion for STEM in our girls from the minute they walk through our door. STEM lessons start in Reception and continue throughout our Junior School where we unpick assumptions about the sciences and start to unlock the satisfaction and creativity that comes from studying STEM subjects. As a result, science and maths have always attracted a high uptake at A-level at St Mary’s School and many of our girls go on to read these subjects at university along with the applied fields of medicine, engineering and biochemistry.
To further support this drive, we recently opened a dedicated STEM learning lab. This unique space – which is part funded by an alumna – is equipped with everything students need to experiment, explore, design, test and perfect their STEM innovation ideas. Additionally, our girls are entered into national competitions, such as Oxford University’s Bebras Computational Thinking Competition, where their success outstrips national averages.
We have outreach programmes with local museums, institutions and tech businesses, which provide positive STEM role models and opportunities. Most recently, our year six pupils enjoyed a visit to Silverstone – gaining an insight into the world of motor racing and the exciting career pathways that studying STEM subjects can unlock.
Sport is also an integral part of life at St Mary’s School. Recent research, undertaken by Women in Sport, suggests girls tend to lose interest in sport when they leave primary school. Our ‘sport for all’ mantra ensures that all of our girls have the opportunity to take part in physical activities that will benefit their physical and mental health.

These activities also teach them valuable lessons relating to leadership, motivation, teamwork, and respect. To support this, we recently opened a brand new sports ground, which includes a 3G pitch for rubgy and football; artificial all-weather pitches for hockey; netball and tennis courts; athletics facilities, a grass pitch for football and athletics; as well as cricket nets.
St Mary's School
Our hockey team was recently crowned County Champions and our netball team also scooped the title of Girls School Association (GSA) Senior Tournament Winners. Our Rowing Club has also just become British Rowing Affiliated, allowing pupils to take part in national competitions and utilise the support and resources only available to British Affiliated clubs.
Whatever your child’s interests, St Mary’s School really is the place where they can be themselves. Research shows that girls in single-sex schools are less likely to follow gender stereotypes. They select subjects that they enjoy, based on their natural ability – not societal norms, combining physics with photography, chemistry with classics and mathematics with Mandarin. They have stronger academic skills. They demonstrate higher self confidence in the sciences. They are also more politically engaged and express stronger community involvement.
Preschool and Junior School open days take place on the 18th March. The school is also opening up the doors to its Senior School on 10th June for student taster workshops. _www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/visit_

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### St Mary's School, Cambridge is an all-girls, all-through day and boarding school that offers an education rooted in the Catholic faith to students with a broad range of abilities. The only all-girls school in Cambridge, St Mary's has a large international boarding community from Year 5.
Located in central Cambridge, St Mary's enrols a total of 650 girls aged three to 18 years. It has 120 years' expertise in educating girls, saying that "From teaching and pastoral care to school life, everything at St Mary’s is built for girls".
As a member of the Girls’ School Association (GSA), it is _proud of its high numbers of girls studying STEM subjects. In 2019,43.6% studied maths compared to 8.1% nationally, and 35.9% studies biology compared to 9.9% nationally._
The school has _dedicated campuses for its Junior School, Senior School and Sixth Form_ (all within walking distance of each other) offering parents the advantage of an all-through education, as well as smaller learning communities for each stage of their child's learning.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### St Mary's School, Cambridge is an all-girls, all-through day and boarding school that offers an education rooted in the Catholic faith to students with a broad range of abilities. The only all-girls school in Cambridge, St Mary's has a large international boarding community from Year 5.
_St Mary's is proud of its international student community (around 20% of students are from overseas, representing over 30 different countries) and this is felt throughout the school corridors._ A noticeboard displays information relating to different countries, cultures, and identities across the world; a giant map in the dining room displays the countries of origin of students at the school; and girls connect with students worldwide through‘E-twinning’ with other schools and sharing virtual classrooms.
While St Mary's is a Catholic school, it does welcome girls of all faiths and secular backgrounds. All students will be expected to attend weekly lessons in religious studies until Year 11 and complete their GCSE in the subject.
texts.5:
# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Curriculum
Teaching follows a blended curriculum that enriches the National Curriculum for England with _specialist teaching from a young age and a cross-curricular approach to subjects including science, art, geography, and music._
As girls move up the school, the curriculum is split into pre-GCSE (Years 7 -9), GCSE curriculum (Years 10-11), and A Levels (Years 12-13).
There's _a strong focus on science and maths here with students working on STEM-related topics from Reception_. The school has also been recognised by the UK Association for the Promotion of Chinese Education (UKAPCE) as one of the ‘Best Schools’ for Mandarin in the UK. Students learn Mandarin during lessons, as well as other traditions such as art and calligraphy, drama and singing.
What are the fees?
attach_money
Average school fees are **GBP 6,300** per year. Additional charges may include registration, enrolment and transport fees.

There are also many extra-curricular clubs focusing on STEM, and scholarships for excellence in Textiles, STEM, and Design and Enterprise.
While St Mary's is a selective school, it does welcome a broad ability range. Compared to the very academically rigorous and selective nature of the neighbouring Perse School, _St Mary's offers a more relaxed learning environment that will certainly suit some girls more than others._
Girls are taught to have great self-belief in their abilities; _whatever their starting point, they are taught to work hard and aim high. HPL, or High Performance Learning, is embedded in the curriculum throughout the school._ This framework of teaching focuses on advanced thinking skills and learning behaviours to help build 'better brains' – and this is key to the school's message to all learners that they _will_ succeed.
texts.6:
# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Sport and the arts
St Mary's is often talked about more for the arts than sport, although there are opportunities to study both as part of the curriculum and as extra-curricular activities.
_All girls study drama in Years 7 and 8, and can take it as an option at GCSE and A Level._ Highlights in the arts calendar include an outdoor Shakespeare production every year. And there are plenty of extra-curricular clubs (15 of these are dedicated to music every week).Facilities include an art and photography centre, which has four art teaching spaces, a Sixth Form study space, a dark room and a photography studio.
Sport at St Mary's _is driven by a 'sports for all' policy, and focuses on the relationship between sport and "self-worth, confidence and body image in young girls"._ While girls still compete in sports including netball, rowing (it is Cambridge after all, and the school does have its own boathouse) and swimming, there are plenty of opportunities to play and enjoy non-performance activities such as boxercise, gymnastics and Zumba. The school has expanded its sports programme to include many solo pursuits than can be enjoyed for life, with less 'traditional' sports such as kung fu and dance.

texts.7:
# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Academic results
Results at St Mary's are impressive. In 2021, 35% of A Level grades were A*, 81% were A*-A, and 97% were A*-B. 100% were A*- C grades.Subject highlights include particularly strong performances in Spanish, Drama, Further Maths, Music, Greek and Latin with 100% of grades at A*.
In GCSEs, 47% of grades were A*, 66% of were A*-A, and 92% were A*- B grades. At least half of all students gained a grade 9 in the following subjects: History (53%), Art (50%), Class Civ (57%), Latin (55%) and Classical Greek (60%). In Music, 100% grades were the top 9 or 8.
_A measure of its success in helping girls of all abilities reach their goals can be seen in its Value Add results._ In 2021, the school's Value Add scores for GCSE and A Level was 0.7, which means that (on average) it added 0.7 of a grade to every girl's results, across all subjects; this could be the difference between 10 Grade 8s and 10 Grade 9s at GCSE.
_75% of St Mary's subject departments recorded Value Added scores placing them in the top 10% of schools,_ while physics, religious studies and Spanish all achieved the highest value-added scores in the UK.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### **Boarding**
Students can board from Year 5, and the majority who do come from overseas. _The school has one boarding house,Mary Ward House, which is within walking distance of the three schools_. There are around 90+ places available for Years 5-13 boarders, and families are advised to apply early as spaces are limited.
texts.10:
# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Admission and fees
Junior School applicants are assessed throughout the year;Senior School applicants attend an assessment day at the end of January; and Sixth Form applicants receive an offer made on their predicted grades.
_International applicants aged 9.5 years and older take the online UKiset test,_ which is designed for international applicants to British independent schools. UK applicants sit assessments for Years 3 and above.
St Mary's is not a highly selective school though, and _girls with a broad range of academic abilities are offered places. Top grades and academic achievement may not guarantee you a place here as the focus is more on evidence of "individual potential"._
Annual fees range from £10,923 for Reception to Year 2, to £17,031 for Years 7-13. Boarding fees start at £27,600 for Years 5-6 up to £35,301 for Years 7-13.

Many schools, especially those originally founded to educate boys, have a distinctly male culture focused on hierarchy and competition. Some girls thrive in this kind of environment. For others a culture focused on equality and cooperation feels more comfortable and nurturing.
Findings from the 2022 Sunday Times Parent Power rankings back this up. Figures released in December – which compared 2022 A-level and GCSE results with those from 2019 – showed that both private and state single-sex girl schools topped the academic league tables. Additionally, research from South Korea entitled ‘Non-Cognitive Consequences of Single-Sex Schooling’ found that single-sex education improves non-cognitive outcomes for students – particularly girls.
St Mary's School
So, what does St Mary’s School offer? Well, we’ve been educating and empowering girls since 1898, developing engaged, compassionate young women with the aspirations, confidence, and integrity to be themselves and help shape a better world.
texts.1:
From the moment they start at St Mary’s, our girls are taught to dream big and strive to reach their full potential. Supporting and challenging them in equal measure, we encourage them to believe anything is possible and nothing is out of their reach. Through High Performance Learning (HPL), we teach them to understand how they learn, as well as what they learn. The result is excellent academic outcomes and young adults who are curious, community-minded, resilient, and ready to go out and make a positive contribution to society.
Within Cambridge, St Mary’s School all-girls offering is unique. We excel at educating girls, and others agree. Our first-class education status was recently reinforced when we received the highest grade of ‘excellent’ in our ISI (Independent Schools Inspectorate) inspection. We achieved ‘excellent’ in both aspects of the Education Quality Inspection, covering academic achievements and personal development; inspectors praised the quality of our teaching; and parents gave us an outstanding overall satisfaction rate of 98%.
In 2022, we saw an incredibly successful return to public examinations with 66% of GCSE grades awarded at A* or A (9 – 7) and 72% of A-levels at grades A* to B. Our international sixth form students recently received outstanding results in their International English Language Testing System (IELTS) examinations.
We’ve also been named one of the best places to study Mandarin in the UK. Inspectors noted at our recent ISI Inspection that: _‘_Pupils make strong progress across the range of subjects’ and are: ‘…highly successful in their achievements beyond the classroom in a range of activities encompassing different interests.’
St Mary's School
The secret to our success is student happiness. We know contented girls accomplish so much more and ensure our pastoral care is second-to-none. Our approach is grounded in love, respect and trust and delivered in a secure environment where students are encouraged to gain a sense of their own worth. When it comes to emotional well-being, students have access to a fully-trained school counsellor, who offers confidential advice.
texts.2:
We also have a Lay Chaplain, who provides a listening ear and wise counsel when needed. The school has an independent listener, who is there for students should they wish to talk to an adult that is independent of the school. Our Senior School pupils can also use our ‘Wellbeing Room’ – immersing themselves in a range of activities and drop-in sessions, in a relaxing space that was designed by our student-led Wellbeing Committee.
At St Mary’s School, all subjects are ‘for girls’. In a nurturing, supportive environment, students are encouraged to pursue their interests, with no academic path off limits. We offer a space where the intellectual and social confidence of our students can blossom and where they can discover what motivates them – supported by excellent careers advice and work experience opportunities.
We work particularly hard to instil them with a passion for maths and science; subjects that girls have historically been less keen to pursue, particularly in co-ed settings.
St Mary's School
We embed a passion for STEM in our girls from the minute they walk through our door. STEM lessons start in Reception and continue throughout our Junior School where we unpick assumptions about the sciences and start to unlock the satisfaction and creativity that comes from studying STEM subjects. As a result, science and maths have always attracted a high uptake at A-level at St Mary’s School and many of our girls go on to read these subjects at university along with the applied fields of medicine, engineering and biochemistry.
To further support this drive, we recently opened a dedicated STEM learning lab. This unique space – which is part funded by an alumna – is equipped with everything students need to experiment, explore, design, test and perfect their STEM innovation ideas. Additionally, our girls are entered into national competitions, such as Oxford University’s Bebras Computational Thinking Competition, where their success outstrips national averages.
We have outreach programmes with local museums, institutions and tech businesses, which provide positive STEM role models and opportunities. Most recently, our year six pupils enjoyed a visit to Silverstone – gaining an insight into the world of motor racing and the exciting career pathways that studying STEM subjects can unlock.
Sport is also an integral part of life at St Mary’s School. Recent research, undertaken by Women in Sport, suggests girls tend to lose interest in sport when they leave primary school. Our ‘sport for all’ mantra ensures that all of our girls have the opportunity to take part in physical activities that will benefit their physical and mental health.
texts.3:
These activities also teach them valuable lessons relating to leadership, motivation, teamwork, and respect. To support this, we recently opened a brand new sports ground, which includes a 3G pitch for rubgy and football; artificial all-weather pitches for hockey; netball and tennis courts; athletics facilities, a grass pitch for football and athletics; as well as cricket nets.
St Mary's School
Our hockey team was recently crowned County Champions and our netball team also scooped the title of Girls School Association (GSA) Senior Tournament Winners. Our Rowing Club has also just become British Rowing Affiliated, allowing pupils to take part in national competitions and utilise the support and resources only available to British Affiliated clubs.
Whatever your child’s interests, St Mary’s School really is the place where they can be themselves. Research shows that girls in single-sex schools are less likely to follow gender stereotypes. They select subjects that they enjoy, based on their natural ability – not societal norms, combining physics with photography, chemistry with classics and mathematics with Mandarin. They have stronger academic skills. They demonstrate higher self confidence in the sciences. They are also more politically engaged and express stronger community involvement.
Preschool and Junior School open days take place on the 18th March. The school is also opening up the doors to its Senior School on 10th June for student taster workshops. _www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/visit_

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### St Mary's School, Cambridge is an all-girls, all-through day and boarding school that offers an education rooted in the Catholic faith to students with a broad range of abilities. The only all-girls school in Cambridge, St Mary's has a large international boarding community from Year 5.
_St Mary's is proud of its international student community (around 20% of students are from overseas, representing over 30 different countries) and this is felt throughout the school corridors._ A noticeboard displays information relating to different countries, cultures, and identities across the world; a giant map in the dining room displays the countries of origin of students at the school; and girls connect with students worldwide through‘E-twinning’ with other schools and sharing virtual classrooms.
While St Mary's is a Catholic school, it does welcome girls of all faiths and secular backgrounds. All students will be expected to attend weekly lessons in religious studies until Year 11 and complete their GCSE in the subject.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Curriculum
Teaching follows a blended curriculum that enriches the National Curriculum for England with _specialist teaching from a young age and a cross-curricular approach to subjects including science, art, geography, and music._
As girls move up the school, the curriculum is split into pre-GCSE (Years 7 -9), GCSE curriculum (Years 10-11), and A Levels (Years 12-13).
There's _a strong focus on science and maths here with students working on STEM-related topics from Reception_. The school has also been recognised by the UK Association for the Promotion of Chinese Education (UKAPCE) as one of the ‘Best Schools’ for Mandarin in the UK. Students learn Mandarin during lessons, as well as other traditions such as art and calligraphy, drama and singing.

While St Mary's is a selective school, it does welcome a broad ability range. Compared to the very academically rigorous and selective nature of the neighbouring Perse School, _St Mary's offers a more relaxed learning environment that will certainly suit some girls more than others._
Girls are taught to have great self-belief in their abilities; _whatever their starting point, they are taught to work hard and aim high. HPL, or High Performance Learning, is embedded in the curriculum throughout the school._ This framework of teaching focuses on advanced thinking skills and learning behaviours to help build 'better brains' – and this is key to the school's message to all learners that they _will_ succeed.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Sport and the arts
St Mary's is often talked about more for the arts than sport, although there are opportunities to study both as part of the curriculum and as extra-curricular activities.
_All girls study drama in Years 7 and 8, and can take it as an option at GCSE and A Level._ Highlights in the arts calendar include an outdoor Shakespeare production every year. And there are plenty of extra-curricular clubs (15 of these are dedicated to music every week).Facilities include an art and photography centre, which has four art teaching spaces, a Sixth Form study space, a dark room and a photography studio.
Sport at St Mary's _is driven by a 'sports for all' policy, and focuses on the relationship between sport and "self-worth, confidence and body image in young girls"._ While girls still compete in sports including netball, rowing (it is Cambridge after all, and the school does have its own boathouse) and swimming, there are plenty of opportunities to play and enjoy non-performance activities such as boxercise, gymnastics and Zumba. The school has expanded its sports programme to include many solo pursuits than can be enjoyed for life, with less 'traditional' sports such as kung fu and dance.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Academic results
Results at St Mary's are impressive. In 2021, 35% of A Level grades were A*, 81% were A*-A, and 97% were A*-B. 100% were A*- C grades.Subject highlights include particularly strong performances in Spanish, Drama, Further Maths, Music, Greek and Latin with 100% of grades at A*.

_A measure of its success in helping girls of all abilities reach their goals can be seen in its Value Add results._ In 2021, the school's Value Add scores for GCSE and A Level was 0.7, which means that (on average) it added 0.7 of a grade to every girl's results, across all subjects; this could be the difference between 10 Grade 8s and 10 Grade 9s at GCSE.
_75% of St Mary's subject departments recorded Value Added scores placing them in the top 10% of schools,_ while physics, religious studies and Spanish all achieved the highest value-added scores in the UK.

# St Mary's School, Cambridge: Review
### Admission and fees
Junior School applicants are assessed throughout the year;Senior School applicants attend an assessment day at the end of January; and Sixth Form applicants receive an offer made on their predicted grades.
_International applicants aged 9.5 years and older take the online UKiset test,_ which is designed for international applicants to British independent schools. UK applicants sit assessments for Years 3 and above.

Title: St Mary’s School on Why There is Still a Place For Single-Sex Education
Chunks: 0,1,2,3
Last year an article examined the future of single-sex schooling and questioned if all-girls schools are a dying breed. The piece followed the news that Scotland’s last all-girls state school has begun enrolling boys. Scotland now has just six single-sex mainstream private schools, and numbers in England are also declining.
Government figures from 2002 showed England had 335 independent all-girls’ schools and 231 girls’ state schools. In 2022 that number fell to 232 and 213 respectively. So, does this downward trend mean single-sex education is outdated and unnecessary?
At St Mary’s School we would argue to the contrary. There are countless benefits to an all-girls education and, until we live in a world where gender inequalities do not exist, we must prepare our girls accordingly.
*   To teach academic subject knowledge, skills and understanding of the wider world and to look outward. This is relatively straight-forward with good teachers and appropriate facilities.

*   To teach self-knowledge and self-understanding and help each individual develop self-worth.
Both of these aspects of education – but particularly the latter – are determined by having the right kind of school culture in place plus a well-defined ethos and mission alongside superb pastoral skills and dedicated tutors. Many schools, especially those originally founded to educate boys, have a distinctly male culture focused on hierarchy and competition. Some girls thrive in this kind of environment. For others a culture focused on equality and cooperation feels more comfortable and nurturing.
Findings from the 2022 Sunday Times Parent Power rankings back this up. Figures released in December – which compared 2022 A-level and GCSE results with those from 2019 – showed that both private and state single-sex girl schools topped the academic league tables. Additionally, research from South Korea entitled ‘Non-Cognitive Consequences of Single-Sex Schooling’ found that single-sex education improves non-cognitive outcomes for students – particularly girls.
St Mary's School
So, what does St Mary’s School offer? Well, we’ve been educating and empowering girls since 1898, developing engaged, compassionate young women with the aspirations, confidence, and integrity to be themselves and help shape a better world.

From the moment they start at St Mary’s, our girls are taught to dream big and strive to reach their full potential. Supporting and challenging them in equal measure, we encourage them to believe anything is possible and nothing is out of their reach. Through High Performance Learning (HPL), we teach them to understand how they learn, as well as what they learn. The result is excellent academic outcomes and young adults who are curious, community-minded, resilient, and ready to go out and make a positive contribution to society.
Within Cambridge, St Mary’s School all-girls offering is unique. We excel at educating girls, and others agree. Our first-class education status was recently reinforced when we received the highest grade of ‘excellent’ in our ISI (Independent Schools Inspectorate) inspection. We achieved ‘excellent’ in both aspects of the Education Quality Inspection, covering academic achievements and personal development; inspectors praised the quality of our teaching; and parents gave us an outstanding overall satisfaction rate of 98%.
In 2022, we saw an incredibly successful return to public examinations with 66% of GCSE grades awarded at A* or A (9 – 7) and 72% of A-levels at grades A* to B. Our international sixth form students recently received outstanding results in their International English Language Testing System (IELTS) examinations.
We’ve also been named one of the best places to study Mandarin in the UK. Inspectors noted at our recent ISI Inspection that: _‘_Pupils make strong progress across the range of subjects’ and are: ‘…highly successful in their achievements beyond the classroom in a range of activities encompassing different interests.’
St Mary's School
The secret to our success is student happiness. We know contented girls accomplish so much more and ensure our pastoral care is second-to-none. Our approach is grounded in love, respect and trust and delivered in a secure environment where students are encouraged to gain a sense of their own worth. When it comes to emotional well-being, students have access to a fully-trained school counsellor, who offers confidential advice.

We also have a Lay Chaplain, who provides a listening ear and wise counsel when needed. The school has an independent listener, who is there for students should they wish to talk to an adult that is independent of the school. Our Senior School pupils can also use our ‘Wellbeing Room’ – immersing themselves in a range of activities and drop-in sessions, in a relaxing space that was designed by our student-led Wellbeing Committee.
At St Mary’s School, all subjects are ‘for girls’. In a nurturing, supportive environment, students are encouraged to pursue their interests, with no academic path off limits. We offer a space where the intellectual and social confidence of our students can blossom and where they can discover what motivates them – supported by excellent careers advice and work experience opportunities.
We work particularly hard to instil them with a passion for maths and science; subjects that girls have historically been less keen to pursue, particularly in co-ed settings.
St Mary's School
We embed a passion for STEM in our girls from the minute they walk through our door. STEM lessons start in Reception and continue throughout our Junior School where we unpick assumptions about the sciences and start to unlock the satisfaction and creativity that comes from studying STEM subjects. As a result, science and maths have always attracted a high uptake at A-level at St Mary’s School and many of our girls go on to read these subjects at university along with the applied fields of medicine, engineering and biochemistry.
To further support this drive, we recently opened a dedicated STEM learning lab. This unique space – which is part funded by an alumna – is equipped with everything students need to experiment, explore, design, test and perfect their STEM innovation ideas. Additionally, our girls are entered into national competitions, such as Oxford University’s Bebras Computational Thinking Competition, where their success outstrips national averages.
We have outreach programmes with local museums, institutions and tech businesses, which provide positive STEM role models and opportunities. Most recently, our year six pupils enjoyed a visit to Silverstone – gaining an insight into the world of motor racing and the exciting career pathways that studying STEM subjects can unlock.
Sport is also an integral part of life at St Mary’s School. Recent research, undertaken by Women in Sport, suggests girls tend to lose interest in sport when they leave primary school. Our ‘sport for all’ mantra ensures that all of our girls have the opportunity to take part in physical activities that will benefit their physical and mental health.

These activities also teach them valuable lessons relating to leadership, motivation, teamwork, and respect. To support this, we recently opened a brand new sports ground, which includes a 3G pitch for rubgy and football; artificial all-weather pitches for hockey; netball and tennis courts; athletics facilities, a grass pitch for football and athletics; as well as cricket nets.
St Mary's School
Our hockey team was recently crowned County Champions and our netball team also scooped the title of Girls School Association (GSA) Senior Tournament Winners. Our Rowing Club has also just become British Rowing Affiliated, allowing pupils to take part in national competitions and utilise the support and resources only available to British Affiliated clubs.
Whatever your child’s interests, St Mary’s School really is the place where they can be themselves. Research shows that girls in single-sex schools are less likely to follow gender stereotypes. They select subjects that they enjoy, based on their natural ability – not societal norms, combining physics with photography, chemistry with classics and mathematics with Mandarin. They have stronger academic skills. They demonstrate higher self confidence in the sciences. They are also more politically engaged and express stronger community involvement.
Preschool and Junior School open days take place on the 18th March. The school is also opening up the doors to its Senior School on 10th June for student taster workshops. _www.stmaryscambridge.co.uk/visit_

Title: Independent Schools of the Year 2024: meet the schools
Chunks: 9,10,11,12,13,14
MHSG is a proudly single-sex school fostering a love for education, lifelong learning, and academic excellence. It emphasises holistic development; encouraging mindfulness, fun, and happiness as key to success. Guided by its core values – Compassion, Individuality, Innovation, Learning, and Wellbeing – it creates a nurturing, inclusive environment.Its 2024 ISI Inspection Report highlighted a “Significant Strength”. Inspectors noted: “Leaders have high aspirations and have firmly established core values that underpin the school. This results in a caring, inclusive and diverse community. Staff are ambitious for the pupils and thread the values of learning, innovation, compassion, wellbeing, and individuality through every aspect of school life. This results in empowered and dynamic pupils who flourish.” It celebrates multi-faith festivals, cultural histories, and raises substantial funds for charity, including a Bursary Fund.It celebrated the school’s 150th Birthday in 2024 and is fundraising to expand its Bursary Fund and introduce new facilities. With a proud history of educating remarkable women, including notable alumni like the Pankhurst sisters, it continues to inspire fearless pioneers. Its curriculum evolves with innovative subjects and with outstanding academic results and strong alumni ties, MHSG remains committed to empowering girls to excel for the next 150 years and beyond.
Find out more at the Manchester High School for Girls website.
**Shortlisted for: Independent School of the Year for Student Well-Being**

The Marist School is ambitious for its girls and in its 55 acre woodland setting, it provides an inspiring education, from nursery through to sixth form, to encourage intellectual curiosity and create a sense of belonging.Its heritage is important and provides a strong foundation on which to grow its vibrant and happy community. Its girls are adventurous, they are kind, they are determined, they champion one another.As important as grades are, education is about much more and in today’s world, young people need more too. As a proudly small school, it is able to adapt its curriculum to ensure that, from an early age, students acquire skills which transcend the standard curriculum. Be that developing new skills through the Marist Diploma Programme; embracing the leadership opportunities; the higher level cognitive skills in Aim Higher; or the extensive enrichment and co-curricular programmes afforded all students through prep and senior.The school is delighted to have been shortlisted for the ISOTY Student Wellbeing award after launching its ‘Wellbeing 2.0’ Framework in 2022, with the goal of ensuring that an excellent collective experience sits at the heart of all that it does.
Find out more at The Marist School website.
**Shortlisted for: Independent Prep School of the Year and Independent School of the Year for Student Well-Being**
Oxford High Prep School GDST is a place where exploration and excellence come together to empower future-ready girls who truly know themselves, find their voices, and use them to make a difference. Fun and friendships go hand in hand with academic achievement. At Oxford High Prep School, the ‘how’ of learning matters as much as the ‘what,’ with teachers often guiding the girls as they take charge of their own learning.The unique curriculum, featuring Global Studies, Earth Studies, and Mandarin, encourages exploration of diversity, inclusion, global citizenship, and living in a more sustainable world. Learning goes far beyond the classroom, with a rich calendar of trips, visits, and clubs that help each girl discover and develop her individual strengths and interests. The Future Ready Programme, shaped by the girls themselves, focuses on nurturing well-rounded, confident pupils across four key areas: self-management, wellness, relationships and learning. Activities range from making jam tarts to writing letters and even opening a bank account – each tailored to the girls’ ages and needs. With pupils recently participating in a Youth TEDx talk, Oxford High Prep School pupils are already shaping the world and building a strong foundation for exciting futures ahead.

Find out more at the Oxford High School GDST website.
**Shortlisted for: Independent Girls’ School of the Year and Independent Prep School of the Year**
Pembridge Hall is a leading all girls prep school in Notting Hill London. Having been founded in 1979 it has developed into an outstanding school, where girls are encouraged to be aspirational in their views, and ambitions, and believe that whatever your gender, you can achieve great things.Pembridge Hall combines traditional values with an innovative and modern education: a Pembridge Hall education is aspirational for, and champions, girls encouraging them in all areas of life and providing them with enriching opportunities.It is a school where sound mental health and wellbeing are at the core of all that it does and will always remain a focus, in turn enabling girls to be the best they can be academically. Pembridge is proof that, despite a broad range of abilities, it is academically ambitious for every girl. Its senior school results consistently demonstrate their exceptional progress over seven years.No girl is made to feel that there is a ceiling to her ability and the enriching academic offering, which develops the girls across a wide range of subject areas, encourages enquiring minds and enables every girl to flourish and succeed as an individual.
Find out more at the Pembridge Hall school website.
**Shortlisted for: Independent Prep School of the Year**

The Ryleys School, located in Alderley Edge, Cheshire, is a distinguished preparatory school with a rich heritage of providing an exceptional education for children aged one to 11. Founded in 1877 on the principles of academic excellence, personal development and individual attention, The Ryleys School offers a nurturing and inspiring environment where each child is given the opportunity to flourish and reach its full potential.The school’s curriculum is thoughtfully crafted to cultivate a passion for learning, encompassing a diverse range of specialist subjects including maths, English, French, PE, music, global perspectives and drama. The Ryleys School endeavours to instil leadership skills, emotional intelligence, and a strong sense of social responsibility in its pupils resulting in a track record of consistent success at 11+ entrance exams.Class sizes are small, and the school has modern and well-equipped facilities, including spacious classrooms, a swimming pool, extensive playing fields, fully equipped science laboratory and large art and design studio. Complementing these resources is a team of dedicated and knowledgeable teachers who provide personalised support to each child, ensuring they receive the guidance, support and encouragement needed to excel. The Ryleys School is a place where young minds are nurtured, inspired, and empowered.
Find out more at The Ryleys School website.
**Shortlisted for: British International School of the Year**

“Rugby School Thailand never stands still. The School is now fully established after 7 years and is thriving”. (COBIS 2024)Rugby School Thailand (RST) is a leading British international day and boarding school for two to 18 year-olds, directly connected to its namesake, Rugby School in the UK. The British values at the heart of RST bring together an international community of 40+ nationalities and the School is passionate about ensuring the English National Curriculum remains relevant within its cultural context.The stunning 80-acre countryside campus is only 70 minutes from Bangkok’s main international airport and 20 minutes from the coast. Strong academics are balanced with a vibrant sports, arts, and enrichment program, with a consistent focus on developing human traits that serve children through life. The extended school day, partnered with the expansive campus and impressive facilities, ensures students have both the time and space to embrace the school’s ethos of “The Whole Person, The Whole Point”, which ultimately improves outcomes for each individual.During accreditation, COBIS noted RST to be “truly exceptional”. In its 2024 review, they said “Rugby School Thailand is amongst a tiny handful of COBIS schools with a double Beacon status. It continues to live up to its excellent reputation”.
Find out more at the Rugby School Thailand website.
**Shortlisted for: Independent Pre-Prep School of the Year**

St John’s College School is a leading independent co-educational day and boarding school in Cambridge which offers an exceptional educational experience to children aged four to 13. At St John’s it aims to foster the aptitudes and nurture the growth of each child to enable them to become their best selves in the fullest sense. It sets its aspirations high through the underlying principle of instilling a love of learning that will stay with them throughout the rest of their lives.It wants its children to become great learners who will go out into our complex and ever-changing world with confidence and the skills they need to make a positive difference. Its rich and varied curriculum with a wide variety of activities allows children to explore and to gain an understanding of the world around them whilst at the same time discovering their strengths and weaknesses. Each child is encouraged to think for him or herself and to continue asking that all-important question ‘why?’. A genuine love of learning together with inspirational teaching in a caring and happy environment leads to exceptional results. This is what the school strives to achieve and is what makes it a very special place.
Find out more at the St Johns College School website.
**Shortlisted for: Independent School of the Year for Diversity, Equality, Inclusion and Justice (DEIJ)**

**St Mary's School, Cambridge** appears to be the only school meeting ALL your requirements (all-girls, independent, Cambridge area, Excellent rating, Mandarin taught). 1. Primary age acceptance and capacity
